# Local autosave and version history

JusPrin saves authored projects in the application data directory under
`jusprin/projects/<project-id>/`. The project ID is independent of the source
filename. Opening an external 3MF or model imports it into a managed draft;
autosave never overwrites the source. **Saved** means the printable
project checkpoint and the current JusPrin document are durable. A 3MF is written
to a user-selected path only through **Export project 3MF…**. A copied 3MF does
not include local versions, conversations, or attachments.

The project header's actions menu exposes the save state, version history,
recent local projects, and export. Version history restores an earlier model
and its effective project settings. The native window title shows the managed
project name and the same save state as the header. Orca's dirty asterisk
does not represent whether the local project has been saved. Before restoring,
JusPrin saves and pins
the current version, then records the restore as a new version, so the prior
state remains available. Each older timestamp has a separate Restore button;
clicking the timestamp does nothing, and Restore asks for confirmation. A blank authored project gets one empty baseline
version so it can be reopened; later document edits do not add versions. A
first Agent model operation pins that baseline as its before-version.
Conversations with each chat's intent and plan, audit, and completed print
records remain in the current document; restoring a model marks the active
chat's plan for reassessment. Region descriptions follow the model: each
version records the list it was saved with, and restoring it brings that list
back. Restoring a model does not undo physical prints or change
global printer facts. Agent
mutations save and pin their actual
before-state, then link an after-version and outcome in an operation record.

## Storage and recovery contract

The restoration rules above describe ordinary Version history. **Restore and
resume** is a separate chat transition. Each chat owns its print intent and
plan; the project's current ones are the active chat's. A chat's checkpoint
holds a model-version reference and a structured setup summary of the moment
it was left. Browsing an older chat does not change the working project.
Resuming it saves and pins the outgoing state, restores the model with its
region descriptions, and activates that chat, whose intent and plan never left
it, only after the new document is durable. Other conversations, audit and print
records, and global printer facts remain. This does not add a full project-
document copy to model versions or make document edits create model versions.
Ordinary Version history remains model-only and does not activate an older
chat. An interrupted chat transition leaves a durable pending marker and
blocks that managed project for explicit recovery on restart.

Each model version has Orca backup-format metadata and a manifest of object
resources. It has no copy of the project document. Unchanged object resources are referenced rather
than serialized again. Changed objects are serialized with Orca's split-model
writer into immutable ZIP resources. A renamed object can reuse its resource;
materialization relabels its entry for Orca's native restore loader. Metadata
and each resource are checked for required entries and geometry. The live
Orca backup directory and an imported source file are never version-store
dependencies.

All project records advance one `current-state.json` document without creating
a model version. The document is atomically replaced after 1.5 seconds without
a change, or within 15 seconds during a continuous stream. Agent and project
boundaries wait for the write. Attachments are written once before their
document references become durable; operation records linking before/after
versions are committed once at the operation boundary. A model checkpoint
ensures the current document is durable before it publishes a new `HEAD`.

## Save classification

The autosave controller observes two independent kinds of change. Native
geometry, transforms, paint, plates, and effective project settings can change
what an earlier printable project reconstructs and therefore create a model
version. A change to the region descriptions makes one too, since a version
records them. Document changes, including streamed Agent messages, drafts,
intent, plans, audit records, and print facts, update only the current
document. `docRevision` is a signal to coalesce that write; neither
it nor document contents participate in model-version equality. A workspace
event can prompt a model check, but cannot make unchanged checkpoint content
into a new version.

A project's directory and its lock are created by its first write, so a
blank project nothing was saved for leaves no directory behind. That first
write fails if another instance saved the same project identity in the
meantime. A single writer owns each project through an OS file lock. It writes and
flushes the current document and changed resources before publishing a version directory,
then atomically replaces `HEAD` with the ordered committed-version index.
POSIX also synchronizes containing directories; Windows flushes individual
files and uses `MoveFileExW` with `MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH`. Restart discards
unfinished staging, unindexed versions, unreachable resources, and old
disposable restore directories. If saving
fails, the current model stays open, the header reports a local save failure,
and the next save retries it. A project folder that can no longer be read or
written is such a failure: the version list is read once when the project
opens and then kept in memory, so the Agent page and Version history keep
working from it while every save is refused, and saving resumes on the next
retry once the folder is available again. Home and Recent projects list
projects by reading the projects folder. A project whose folder cannot be
read is left out of the list, like a damaged one. If the projects folder
itself cannot be read, Home says the projects couldn't be loaded instead of
showing an empty gallery, and keeps reading the folder while it is on
screen, so the projects reappear once the folder is readable; the header's
Recent projects menu says they couldn't be loaded. Opening a file while the
projects folder cannot be read stops before anything is replaced, because
whether the file was opened before cannot be told: a person is told so, and
the Agent's `project_open` fails with `local_save_failed` saying why. Project replacement is blocked until the live
state is saved. Explicit export validates a temporary 3MF before replacing
its destination.

Older projects may still contain `Auxiliaries/JusPrin/state.json`. On first adoption, JusPrin reads that state and copies its
attachments to the managed store; it does not delete the old source. Once a
managed version exists, local state is authoritative. Reopening a copied
external 3MF with an already managed identity forks a new project identity.
When a file opened as a project matches a saved project, JusPrin asks whether
to create another project or open the existing one directly. A project
remembers the file it was opened from (`openedFrom`) and that file's MD5 then
(`openedDigest`) in each version manifest: a .3mf from its project path, a model
file the agent's `project_open` opened as a new project from the path it gave.
Every way a person opens a .3mf asks, because the check sits in
`Plater::load_project` (File > Open Project, recent files, Finder, drops); the
agent's `project_open` returns the question as `opened_before` and takes the
answer as `openedBefore`. A file whose MD5 differs is a likely new export, so
the question says so and defaults to a new project; otherwise it defaults to
the saved one. Importing a file into a project never asks. If several
projects match, it continues the current one when it came from that file;
otherwise it opens the most recently updated match.
The project document has one schema version and no migration (the project is
not live yet): a document of any other version, like a corrupt one, is
replaced by a fresh document. The local store reads only its current index,
manifest and current-document formats.
Recent projects appear on Home and in the header menu. Selecting one
opens its managed version even when its imported source file has been removed.
The most recently authored local project resumes on startup.

# 3. Recommended final product structure

The application should use one main window rather than turning every stage of a print into equal global navigation.

## 3.1 Home

Home is the hub for:

- Printer cards showing availability, condition, and loaded filament
- Project gallery, open, and project status
- Import of 3MF, STL, STEP, SVG, OBJ, AMF, and ZIP files
- Entry to project versions and backups
- Launching Monitor

## 3.2 Project window

The Project window contains the print-planning lifecycle without dividing it into equal destinations:

- **Prepare:** dominant workspace containing intent, objects and plates, the 3D canvas, geometry editing, local meaning, and the agent plan

Opening a file that a saved project was made from asks whether to continue

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. input.ask: Should importing a model file from Home, Finder or a drop start a new project?

actions.label: New project
actions.message: Importing a model from Home, Finder or a drop should start a new project. Write up the expected behavior for all three paths on that basis.

actions.label: Add to open project

content.text:
No document says clearly what import should do. The docs and the code also disagree on the main point: whether importing a model file (STL, STEP, OBJ…) starts a **new project** or **adds to the project that's open**. Today every path adds to the open project. Everything below comes from reading the code and docs, plus the log from the session you ran at 05:24. I did not run anything live.

## What the docs say

- **Home is where import lives.** `product-definition.md` §3.1 lists "Import of 3MF, STL, STEP, SVG, OBJ, AMF, and ZIP files" as a Home function. It doesn't say what the import does.
- **Opening a file makes a new project.** `autosave-version-history.md` says: "Opening an external 3MF or model imports it into a managed draft". A managed draft is a new project that autosave keeps, and the source file is never overwritten. The same doc says "Importing a file into a project never asks", so it treats *opening* a file and *importing into a project* as two different actions.
- **A 3MF you've opened before asks first.** The same doc says every way a person opens a .3mf asks "Previously opened file". It lists File › Open Project, recent files, Finder and drops.
- **The code comments read the other way.** The Home backend's comment says "add_model imports into the project that is open". `ShellController.cpp` says "Add-model remains available through File > Import and drag-drop."

## What the code does now

**1. The Import button on Home** (JusPrin's code, `OrcaHomeBackend::import_model`)
- It calls OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, which opens the file dialog and adds the file to the project that's already open. At startup that's the most recent project, which you can't see from Home.
- It switches to Prepare only if the number of objects went up. Cancelling, or a file that brings no objects, leaves you on Home with no message.
- A .3mf picked here only adds its geometry. It is never opened as a project.
- Your 05:24 log matches this. `general_purpose_hook.STL` went into the already-open "Overture PLA Matte" project. `20mmbox…gcode.3mf` added 0 objects, so nothing visible happened.

**2. Opening a file from Finder** (OrcaSlicer's `GUI_App::MacOpenFiles`, unchanged by JusPrin)
- **Model file:** it is added to the open project, the same as Import. Nothing in this path switches away from Home.
- **.3mf:** your config has `single_instance: false`, which is OrcaSlicer's default. So the app runs `open -n` and starts a second JusPrin process with the file, instead of opening it in the window you have.

**3. Drag and drop** (OrcaSlicer's `PlaterDropTarget`)
- Only the 3D view (Prepare) accepts drops. A drop there brings the window forward, switches to Prepare and loads the file.
- **Model file:** it is added to the open project.
- **.3mf on an empty plate:** it opens as a project, and the "Previously opened file" question applies.
- **.3mf on a plate that has objects:** OrcaSlicer would ask "open as project or import geometry". During a person's file open, JusPrin answers OrcaSlicer's dialogs automatically and picks Cancel when there is one. Reading the code, the drop then does nothing. That contradicts the autosave doc, but I haven't seen it happen.
- **Drop onto Home:** Home is a separate web page in front of the 3D view, and it has no drop handling. What happens there is untested.
- **Drop onto the Agent panel:** the file is attached to the chat. That one is deliberate.

All three paths go through the same loading code, so the Agent's first message about a loaded file should fire after each of them.

## The decision that settles it

If import should start a new project, then Home Import and opening a model from Finder are both wrong today. Dropping onto Home would then most likely start a new project as well. Dropping onto an open project stays a judgement call: it could add to that project, as now, or start a new one. If import should add to the open project, the code already does that, and what's broken is narrower:
- you can't see from Home which project the file went into;
- a .3mf from Finder starts a second app;
- a .3mf dropped on a non-empty plate is silently cancelled.

I stopped the test copy of the app and the rebuild I had started. Your running JusPrin and the built app (still the Oct 22 build) are untouched. Some of the build's intermediate files were updated before I stopped it, so the next build of `build/arm64` will finish that work.

content.text:
Git history shows two separate problems.

- **Home's Import button:** it was wired to "add to the open project" from the day Home was built. It never opened a file as a project, and no branch ever had it do that.
- **Dropped or opened 3MFs:** these did reach the "Previously opened file" question at first. A change one day later most likely broke that; I found this by reading the code and haven't reproduced it.

These are fork commits; I checked that none of them is on any upstream branch.

## Home's Import button

- **c346a5348e (Sept 12, "Build the Home screen as a fork-owned page")** sent Import to OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, with the comment "add_model imports into the project that is open". `add_model` only ever loads geometry. Even for a .3mf it never opens the file as a project and never asks the "Previously opened file" question.
- **cc017e0b22 (Sept 12)** moved that code into `OrcaHomeBackend::import_model` without changing what it does.
- **076ed1d4c3 (Sept 30, "Add managed project autosave and version history")** is what made it visibly wrong. That commit opens the most recent project again at every startup. Before it, the app started with an empty plate, so importing an STL from Home gave you a project holding just that file. That's probably the behavior you remember. Since Sept 30 there is always a project open behind Home, and Import adds into it, as your 05:24 import did to the Overture project.

## A 3MF dropped on the window or opened from Finder

1. **076ed1d4c3 (Sept 30)** added the "Previously opened file" check. It sat on the branch where OrcaSlicer opens a 3MF as a project. On an empty plate that happens directly. On a plate that already has objects, OrcaSlicer first asks whether to open the file as a project or import only its geometry, and you reached the check by choosing "open as project".
2. **832bb47c31 (Oct 1, "Report file-opening notices in the Agent's first message")** made JusPrin answer every OrcaSlicer dialog that appears while a person opens a file, picking Cancel whenever there is one. That "project or geometry" dialog has a Cancel button, so the open is now cancelled without you seeing anything. Because of the Sept 30 change the plate is almost never empty, so from Oct 1 a dropped 3MF most likely does nothing.
3. **849b2b516a (Oct 14)** moved the "Previously opened file" check into `Plater::load_project`. That doesn't help here, because the cancelled dialog stops the open before `load_project` runs.

## What has always been OrcaSlicer's behavior

- A model file (STL, STEP, OBJ…) that is dropped or opened from Finder is added to the open project.
- A 3MF opened from Finder starts a second app process. This is because `single_instance` is false, OrcaSlicer's default on the Mac.

Neither of these follows your expected behavior either. Neither one is a recent regression.

The "Add-model remains available through File > Import and drag-drop" comment in `ShellController.cpp` dates from Aug 30. It is about the toolbar the shell hides over the 3D view, not about Home.

Let's figure out what an optimal user experience should be. We don't have to be limited to current documented behavior or implemented behavior. For instance, we can be open about what buttons we need for on the homepage or if we need any buttons at all. Based on how user usually opens a file as well as how they would expect an app to behave upon such an action.

Here's how I'd reason about it, starting from how people actually bring files in and what they expect to happen, then what that implies for Home.

## How a file arrives, and what the person means by it

There are really only four ways, and they carry different intent:

1. **Double-click in Finder, or "Open with JusPrin" from a browser download.** The person has a file and wants to *work on it*. They are not thinking about whatever JusPrin had open; often they haven't looked at JusPrin yet. Every Mac app treats this as "show me this document."
2. **Drag from Finder onto the app.** Same intent as 1 when dropped on the window in general or the Dock icon. One exception: dropping onto a plate that already has parts on it reads as "put this *here*", because the person is aiming at a specific place.
3. **A button or menu inside the app** (Open…, Cmd+O, File › Import). Intent follows the label. "Open" means work on this; "Import" or "Add" means into what I have.
4. **Through the agent chat** (the + button, or dropping onto the pane). Already handled: it attaches, and the agent adds it to the open project.

So the split is **"start from this file"** versus **"add this to what I'm doing"**. The second is real (multi-part prints) but is the minority case, and the person usually signals it by aiming at the plate or by asking the agent.

## Why "start a new project" is the safe default

Autosave changes the trade-off. Nothing is ever lost when the open project is replaced, so starting a new project wrongly costs the person one click on Recent. Adding to the open project wrongly is worse: their old project now has a stray part in it, and they have to delete it and then open the file again the way they meant to. That is exactly what happened at 05:24 with the Overture project. When the cheap mistake and the expensive mistake are on different sides, default to the cheap one.

A model file always makes a new project. A 3MF makes a new project too, with the one question JusPrin already keeps: if that file was opened before, continue the existing project or create another.

## Proposed behavior per path

| Path | Model file (STL, STEP, OBJ, …) | 3MF |
|---|---|---|
| Finder / browser "open with" | New project, go to Prepare | New project; ask if opened before |
| Drop on Home, or on the window chrome | New project, go to Prepare | Same |
| Drop on the Prepare canvas | Add to the open project (as today) | New project; ask if opened before |
| Home's open button | New project | Same |
| Agent + / drop on the pane | Attach, agent adds to the open project | Attach |

Two things that need to change in OrcaSlicer's behavior for this to hold: a 3MF from Finder must land in this window instead of launching a second JusPrin (the `single_instance` setting), and the "open as project or just import geometry?" dialog goes away for 3MFs, since the table above already answers it. A 3MF dropped on the plate with "I only want its geometry" is rare, and the agent can do that on request.

Multiple files dropped together go into one new project. G-code files are a separate question (OrcaSlicer opens a viewer); I'd leave them as they are for now.

## What Home needs

Today Home has "Import" and "+ New". I'd change both:

- **"Import" is the wrong word.** It implies "into something", and there is nothing on Home to import into. Call it **Open…** (Cmd+O). It opens the file dialog and the result is a new project.
- **Home is the drop target.** The whole page accepts a dropped file and says so softly in the empty state ("Drop a model or project here, or Open…"). Most people arrive with a file in hand; this is the one gesture that needs no reading.
- **"+ New" (blank project) can go, or become secondary.** Nobody designs in a slicer, so a blank plate is a starting point only for calibration prints and for "I'll add parts one by one". The calibration flow starts its own project already. If you want to keep it, put it in the header menu or as a text link, not beside Open.

So Home becomes: printers, recent projects, one primary action (Open…), and the page itself as the drop zone.

## Two things I'd want you to decide

1. **A model file dropped on the Prepare canvas: add to the open project, or new project?** I recommend *add*, because the person aimed at the plate and that is what every slicer does. The alternative, *new project everywhere*, is simpler to explain but takes away the only no-chat way to add a part.
2. **A 3MF dropped on the Prepare canvas: new project, or keep OrcaSlicer's "project or geometry?" question?** I recommend *new project with no question*. The cases where someone wants the geometry out of a 3MF are rare enough to go through the agent.

One thing I haven't verified: whether the app lands on Home or on the resumed project at startup. That decides whether the first drop a person makes after launch lands on Home or on a canvas, so it's worth settling as part of this.

# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.

### Canvas presentation

`GLCanvas3D` keeps a small API for controlling how its parts are presented. That API contains nothing specific to JusPrin. A controller in fork-owned code uses the API to apply JusPrin's choices, and puts OrcaSlicer's previous state back when the controller is destroyed. Whether a control is drawn and whether it receives input must be two separate switches. Otherwise a control that is hidden could still swallow pointer events. OrcaSlicer's native gizmos (the on-canvas tools such as Move and Rotate) must stay usable while one is active.

The Check print window's preview has its own controller, `PreviewPresentationController` beside `CanvasPresentationController`. It hides the canvas's legacy overlay layer (plate selector strip, 3D navigator, canvas toolbar), holds OrcaSlicer's app-wide G-code listing preference (`show_gcode_window`) off while the window is open, and switches the legend through `GCodeViewer::show_legend`; destroying it restores all three, on every close path. Both sliders stay as OrcaSlicer draws them. OrcaSlicer's single ImGui context also keeps the last pointer position of whichever canvas saw it, so the window clears it when it opens and when the pointer leaves its canvas.

The POC had one broad switch, `render_overlays`. Production needs finer control. Treat each of these as its own item that can be shown or hidden separately: OrcaSlicer's main toolbar, the gizmo picker, the handles of the active gizmo, plate actions, object labels, layer-editing controls, navigation aids, the Preview legend, and the Preview sliders. Some controls are shared between canvases, such as `Plater`'s collapse toolbar. A shared control must be saved and restored by one object that lives as long as the shell does. Do not give each canvas its own guard for it.

### Plates and Project pane

This pane is native code owned by the fork (`Shell/LeftPane`). It sits to the left of the workspace on Prepare. Its first tab lists every plate, even when the project has only one. Its second tab shows the saved project's identity, the model's 3MF metadata, the history of physical prints, the version history, and export. The pane keeps no project state of its own and has no undo of its own. It draws what two model classes describe, and those classes do not depend on the GUI. Every click calls a workspace command.

| Piece | What it is responsible for |
|---|---|

# Opening and importing files: code changes per path

Working doc, untracked. The behavior itself is recorded in
`agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md` › "Opening and importing files" (2026-10-24).
This lists what has to change in code to make each path do what that section says,
with the file and function names as they are on `jusprin-newui` at a8a6139841.

## Where every path lands today

All OS and drop paths end in `Plater::load_files(const wxArrayString&)`
(Plater.cpp:14208), which adds a model file to the open project and sends a lone
.3mf through `Plater::open_3mf_file`. Home's Import button ends in
`Plater::add_model` (Plater.cpp:12613), which always adds. The agent's
`project_open` (OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2498) already does "new project named
after the file, then load" and is the model for the shell routine below.

## 0. One fork-owned routine the paths share

`ShellController` (or a small fork-owned helper beside it) gets
`open_files_as_project(const std::vector<fs::path>&)`:

1. If `m_autosave` is missing or `m_workspace->tool_load_active()`, return false
   (a tool's own open is reported by the tool).
2. Split: a lone .3mf → `plater.open_3mf_file(path)`; with `project_load_behaviour`
   set to `load_all` (step 4) that reaches `Plater::load_project(path, "<loadall>")`,
   which runs the existing "Previously opened file" handler
   (`set_external_project_open_handler`, ShellController.cpp:435). Nothing new there.
3. Model files (one or several) → `plater.new_project(true, true, <stem of first file>)`
   (its autosave hook saves the outgoing project; `wxID_CANCEL` means the save failed,
   so stop and show the save-failed message as `project_open` does), then
   `plater.load_files(paths, LoadStrategy::LoadModel)` (the `std::vector<fs::path>`
   overload, which never re-enters the seam in step 1). Drop unsaved preset edits the way
   `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::open_project` does.
4. `m_frame->select_tab(tp3DEditor)` when something loaded. The file-loaded report and
   the Agent's first message already fire through `FileLoadScope`.

Mixed drops (3mf + STL together): open the .3mf as the project, then add the rest,
which is what `Plater::load_files(wxArrayString)` does for `Multiple3MFOther` today.

## 1. Opened from the OS (Finder, Explorer, "Open with", a second launch)

Entry points, all OrcaSlicer-owned, all ending in `load_files(wxArrayString)`:

- macOS: `GUI_App::MacOpenFiles` (GUI_App.cpp:8601) → `plater()->load_files(input_files)`.
- Windows/Linux, app already running: `OtherInstanceMessageHandler::handle_message`
  (InstanceCheck.cpp:482) posts `EVT_LOAD_MODEL_OTHER_INSTANCE`; Plater.cpp:5444 handles it
  with `load_files(input_files)`.
- Any platform, launched with files: `GUI_App::post_init` (GUI_App.cpp:785).

The behavior is recorded and the code-change list is written. Nothing is committed yet.

## Your question: how does someone find "add a part to this project"?

The research says the same thing across slicers: the drag-onto-the-plate gesture is never the only way. Each one keeps a control *inside the workspace* that is always on screen:

- **PrusaSlicer** has an Add button on the top toolbar, and separates Ctrl+O (open a project, clear the plate) from Ctrl+I (import a model, keep the plate).
- **Cura** has a folder icon at the top left of Prepare; drag and drop is listed as the extra, not the main, way.
- **OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio** have an Add button on the main toolbar. JusPrin hides that toolbar, which is why the gap exists for us and not for them.

So the answer is to give JusPrin the same shape: an **Add model…** button at the top of the Plates tab in the Plates and Project pane (that's where the objects are listed, so it's where a person looks when thinking "I want another one here"), plus the paths that already exist: File › Import (Cmd+I), the composer's + › 3D model, asking the agent, and the drop. The empty plate gets a hint ("Drop a model here or add one"). I'd stop there; a dedicated toolbar is more than this case warrants.

## What I wrote

- [architecture.md](agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md): a new "Opening and importing files" section with the table of every way a file arrives and what it does, the rules that follow, the discoverability answer, and who owns what (policy fork-owned; one additive seam in OrcaSlicer plus two of its own settings, `single_instance` and `project_load_behaviour`).
- [autosave-version-history.md](agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md): the paragraph on which ways ask the "Previously opened file" question now lists Home's Open… and drops on Home, and distinguishes opening from adding.
- [product-definition.md](agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md): §3.1 says Home opens files as new projects rather than "imports" them.
- [import-behavior-code-changes.md](import-behavior-code-changes.md) (untracked, repo root): the per-path code changes. The short version:
  1. **OS open** (Finder, Explorer, second launch): one additive seam in `Plater::load_files(const wxArrayString&)`, a `set_external_file_open_handler` mirroring the project hook that already exists; the shell installs a routine that does new-project-then-load, modeled on the agent's `project_open`. Plus `single_instance=true` written from fork-owned config code.
  2. **Home Open…**: rename the message, swap `add_model` for the OS dialog plus that same routine.
  3. **Canvas drop**: a fork-owned drop target so a model still adds while a 3MF opens as a project; `project_load_behaviour=load_all` so OrcaSlicer never asks "project or geometry?", which also removes the silent cancel from Oct 1.
  4. **Home drop**: needs a spike first. The web view probably swallows drags, and a page-side drop gives bytes without a path.
  5. **Add model…** button in the Plates pane; File › Import and the composer + already work.
  6. Tests and harness checks to add, and the design boards still showing "Import" / "+ New".

One thing left open in the doc: whether the app lands on Home or on the resumed project at launch. That decides what the first drop after launch hits, so it's worth settling before the Home-drop work.
